arxiv-2302-11472.title: Distilling Calibrated Student from an Uncalibrated Teacher
arxiv-2302-11472.creator: Ishan Mishra, Sethu Vamsi Krishna, Deepak Mishra
arxiv-2302-11472.description: Abstract Knowledge distillation is a common technique for improving the performance of a shallow student network by transferring information from a teacher network, which in general, is comparatively large and deep. These teacher networks are pre-trained and often uncalibrated, as no calibration technique is applied to the teacher model while training.

arxiv-2408-06756.title: Improving Quantum Developer Experience with Kubernetes and Jupyter Notebooks
arxiv-2408-06756.creator: Otso Kinanen, Andrés D. Muñoz-Moller, Vlad Stirbu, Tommi Mikkonen
arxiv-2408-06756.description: Abstract Quantum computing proposes a revolutionary paradigm that can radically transform numerous scientific and industrial application domains. To realize this promise, new capabilities need software solutions that are able to effectively harness its power. However, developers face significant challenges when developing quantum software due to the high computational demands of simulating quantum computers on classical systems.

arxiv-2409-17283.title: Investigating Privacy Attacks in the Gray-Box Setting to Enhance Collaborative Learning Schemes
arxiv-2409-17283.creator: Federico Mazzone, Ahmad Al Badawi, Yuriy Polyakov, Maarten Everts, Florian Hahn, Andreas Peter
arxiv-2409-17283.description: Abstract The notion that collaborative machine learning can ensure privacy by just withholding the raw data is widely acknowledged to be flawed. Over the past seven years, the literature has revealed several privacy attacks that enable adversaries to extract information about a model’s training dataset by exploiting access to model parameters during or after training.

arxiv-2504-13809.title: A Fast Direct Solver for Boundary Integral Equations Using Quadrature By Expansion
arxiv-2504-13809.creator: Alexandru Fikl 1, Andreas Klöckner 2
arxiv-2504-13809.description: Abstract We construct and analyze a hierarchical direct solver for linear systems arising from the discretization of boundary integral equations using the Quadrature by Expansion (QBX) method. Our scheme builds on the existing theory of Hierarchical Semi-Separable (HSS) matrix operators that contain low-rank off-diagonal submatrices.

arxiv-2510-02916.title: SALSA-V: Shortcut-Augmented Long-form Synchronized Audio from Videos
arxiv-2510-02916.creator: Amir Dellali, Luca A. Lanzendörfer, Florian Grötschla, Roger Wattenhofer
arxiv-2510-02916.description: Abstract We propose SALSA-V, a multimodal video-to-audio generation model capable of synthesizing highly synchronized, high-fidelity long-form audio from silent video content. Our approach introduces a masked diffusion objective, enabling audio-conditioned generation and the seamless synthesis of audio sequences of unconstrained length.

pmc-12613343.title: Virulence patterns of Colletotrichum truncatum isolates causing soybean anthracnose disease and identification of resistance sources
pmc-12613343.creator: Saloni Mandloi, Pooja Dhaka, Vennampally Nataraj, Vibha Pandey, Sanjeev Kumar, Laxman Singh Rajput, Giriraj Kumawat, M. Shivakumar, Palak Solanki, Satish Kumar Nagar, Hemant Singh Maheshwari, Vangala Rajesh, Milind B. Ratnaparkhe, Sanjay Gupta, K. H. Singh
pmc-12613343.description: Anthracnose disease caused by Colletotrichum truncatum is a major disease in soybean in India. In the current study, a total of sixty isolates of C. truncatum were tested for their virulence against three soybean genotypes viz., EC 18,596, JS 20–34, and JS 95 − 60.

pmc-12675314.title: An Equity‐Focused Systematic Analysis of Antimicrobial Resistance National Action Plans in 14 West African Countries
pmc-12675314.creator: Yusuff Adebayo Adebisi, Isaac Olushola Ogunkola, Adeola Bamisaiye, Aminat Olaitan Adebayo, Noah Sesay, Kwasi Yelarge, Don Eliseo Lucero‐Prisno
pmc-12675314.description: ObjectivesAntimicrobial resistance is a growing global health threat that disproportionately affects socially and economically disadvantaged populations. National Action Plans are critical for coordinating national responses, but the extent to which they address equity remains unclear. This study assessed how antimicrobial resistance National Action Plans from 14 West African countries incorporate equity considerations.

pmc-12678120.title: Macrophages in osteoporotic fractures: from immunometabolic mechanisms to precision therapeutic approaches
pmc-12678120.creator: Jiahui Xing, Haibo Li, Honggang Xia, Lilei Xia, Hongzhou Zhao
pmc-12678120.description: Osteoporosis (OP) is a systemic bone disease characterized by reduced bone mass and deterioration of bone microarchitecture. Its critical complication, osteoporotic fractures (OPF), imposes a significant global disease burden. Macrophages, serving as central regulators within the osteoimmune microenvironment, dynamically modulate bone homeostasis and fracture healing through polarization (into pro-inflammatory M1 and reparative M2 phenotypes) and metabolic reprogramming.

pmc-12979852.title: Small RNA sequencing analysis identified miR159a as a novel candidate for activity in plant-derived nanovesicles from limon, hassaku, and sudachi
pmc-12979852.creator: Hideki Takakura, Shingo Miyamoto, Tetsushi Yamamoto, Toshimasa Nakao, Atsushi Taga, Michihiro Mutoh, Keisuke Oda
pmc-12979852.description: Owing to their safety, plant-derived nanovesicles (PDNVs), particularly those derived from edible plants, are expected to be natural delivery carriers for microRNAs (miRNAs). Among PDNVs, Citrus limon-derived extracellular vesicle-like nanovesicles have been shown to exert antitumor effects. We previously reported that PDNVs derived from C. limon L. exert selective inhibitory effects on the proliferation of p53-inactivated colon cancer cells.

pmc-13055795.title: Impact of Coronary Artery Disease Extent on GRACE Risk Score Prognostic Performance After ST‐Segment–Elevation Myocardial Infarction
pmc-13055795.creator: Kayode O. Kuku, Chris Lenselink, Constantijn S. Venema, Hector M. Garcia‐Garcia, Pim van der Harst, Erik Lipsic, Adriaan A. Voors, Joanna J. Wykrzykowska
pmc-13055795.description: BackgroundThe GRACE (Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events) score is well validated for risk stratification in non–ST‐segment–elevation myocardial infarction, but less well established in ST‐segment–elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), particularly relative to coronary disease burden. We therefore assessed its prognostic performance in a STEMI cohort, accounting for baseline coronary disease extent.

pmc-13208427.title: Prediction Models for Frailty in People Living With HIV: Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Prognostic Models
pmc-13208427.creator: Yeye Hu, Meilian Xie, Zhiyun Zhang, Javad Sarvestan
pmc-13208427.description: BackgroundWith the advent of antiretroviral therapy, the life expectancy of people living with HIV has increased significantly, leading to a growing prevalence of frailty and its associated adverse outcomes. However, frailty prediction models developed for the general older population may not apply to people living with HIV due to their distinct immunologic, inflammatory, and comorbidity profiles.

pmc-13431649.title: JAK1-preferential inhibition in refractory inflammatory bowel disease: reframing upadacitinib as a strategy for rapid immune recalibration
pmc-13431649.creator: Xiaowei Liu, Yang Wang
pmc-13431649.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) management has moved from symptom control toward treat-to-target strategies, yet many patients with ulcerative colitis or Crohn’s disease remain difficult to treat after primary non-response, secondary loss of response, or intolerance to advanced therapy. Upadacitinib, an oral Janus kinase 1 (JAK1)-preferential inhibitor, has shown clinically meaningful efficacy in both ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease, including biologic-experienced populations.

pmc-13476402.title: Evaluation of GFAP, UCH-L1 and S100B Blood Biomarkers for the Management of Sports-Related Concussion in Professional Rugby Players: A Prospective Observational Study
pmc-13476402.creator: Charlotte Oris, Rémi Gaulmin, Julie Durif, Vincent Goddelière, Bruno Pereira, Damien Bouvier, Vincent Sapin
pmc-13476402.description: BackgroundThe incidence of sports-related concussion (SRC) in rugby has been rising in recent years. The Head Injury Assessment (HIA) protocol, used to manage SRC, is limited by its reliance on subjective symptom reporting. Blood biomarkers such as glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) and S100B could serve as complementary objective tools for SRC management.

pmc-13584466.title: Depressive and anxiety symptoms in COPD: associations with diffusion impairment and echocardiographic pulmonary hemodynamic burden
pmc-13584466.creator: Tetsuya Hiramoto, Satoshi Izuno, Kenta Toda, Atsushi Moriwaki, Makoto Yoshida
pmc-13584466.description: BackgroundPsychological distress is common yet often underrecognized in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Physiological correlates beyond spirometry may support biopsychosocial assessment in routine care, but their relation to depressive and anxiety symptoms remain insufficiently characterized.MethodsIn this single-center cross-sectional study, 56 clinically stable Japanese COPD outpatients (mean age 73 years; 87.

pmc-13644225.title: The diagnosis and prognosis role of miR-155 in neonatal acute respiratory distress syndrome
pmc-13644225.creator: Yangping Zhou, Yuan Yu, Jiangshan Wang, Meina Sun, Liang Bao, Xin Du, Juan Ouyang
pmc-13644225.description: BackgroundNeonatal acute respiratory distress syndrome (NARDS) can cause respiratory failure in newborns and even pose a threat to their lives, causing a heavy financial burden on families.AimThis study aims to explore the potential role of miR-155 as a diagnostic marker and prognostic predictor for NARDS.MethodsThis study included 100 non-NARDS newborns and 100 NARDS newborns.

pmc-13677708.title: Predicting unknown mammalian viral hosts with Dynamic Positive–Unlabeled learning
pmc-13677708.creator: Gabriele Pignalberi, Andrea Tonelli, Stefano Giagu, Moreno Di Marco
pmc-13677708.description: Most emerging infectious diseases in humans are zoonotic in origin. Yet, knowledge of host–pathogen associations remains limited. Machine learning models have been increasingly used to infer missing zoonotic host–pathogen associations, but face challenges due to biased data and the absence of confirmed negative cases.

pmc-13685271.title: Continuous mechanical compression-induced intervertebral disc degeneration and pain in the caudal spine in rats
pmc-13685271.creator: Fei Chen, Na Li, Junjie Pu, Yiling Deng, Junhui Qi, Fanyi Kong, Jiayu Chen
pmc-13685271.description: BackgroundChronic low back pain imposes substantial social and economic burdens due to its rising prevalence and associated disability. Intervertebral disc degeneration is the primary driver of discogenic back pain, though the mechanistic links between degenerative changes and persistent pain remain incompletely defined. Aberrant mechanical loading is recognised as a key trigger of disc degeneration.
